title: We choose Agni as messenger

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «दूतं देवान् प्रति प्रेषणार्हं», fit to be sent to the gods

words.meaning: the invoker, the priest who calls the gods
skilful in act, wise in counsel

samasa.meaning: whose power of action or of mind is good

morphology.note: √vṛ ‘to choose’, ninth class, middle: the sacrificers choose Agni for themselves.

translation.literal: We choose Agni as messenger, as invoker, all-knowing, skilful in act of this sacrifice.
translation.readable: We choose Agni to be our messenger and to call the gods: he knows all things, and he is skilled in the work of this sacrifice.

meaning: A three-line gāyatrī verse to Agni, the sacrificial fire. The sacrificers choose him for three offices: as messenger (dūta) who carries the offering and the prayer to the gods, as hotṛ who calls the gods to the sacrifice, and as the one skilled in the sacrifice’s work. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (3.5.2) it is the eighth of the sāmidhenī verses, recited while the fire is kindled with sticks at the start of an iṣṭi; it is also the first verse of the Ṛgveda’s twelfth hymn (1.12.1). The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The second mantra of Sūrya’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, addressed to Agni. S recites it with the graha’s own mantra and names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on TB 3.5.2, reads it as the eighth sāmidhenī («अष्टम-सामिधेनी-पाठस् तु») and explains: «इमम् अग्निं वयं वृणीमहे प्रार्थयामहे», with Agni as «दूतं देवान् प्रति प्रेषणार्हं, होतारम् आह्वातारं».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «अग्निं दूतं हितकारिणं सर्वेषां होतारं आह्वातारं विश्ववेदसं विश्वस्य वेदितारं» — the messenger is the one who works for the good of all.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre gāyatrī, three pādas of eight syllables. The Ṛgveda (1.12.1) has the same words.
